description: Investigate why previously valid Meridian thumbnails disappear and regress to letter placeholders while Chrome remains open continuously and the affected tabs remain open, then fix the loss and add non-intrusive recovery. This is confirmed in-session thumbnail loss, not tabs that were never captured and not browser-restart tab-ID churn. The reported state is visible in .tasker/chats/e123bfc1/attachments/Screenshot_2026-07-26_135726.png: many cards that previously showed screenshots lost them, while a newer-looking thumbnail remained. Primary hypotheses to test: - thumbnailCache pruning crosses MAX_BYTES/MAX_ENTRIES and evicts thumbnails belonging to still-open tabs; the pattern of many old placeholders plus a surviving recent capture is consistent with LRU eviction. - thumbnailCacheAccess metadata diverges from actual thumb_* keys or accumulates stale/orphaned entries, producing incorrect byte totals and removals. - Concurrent save/evict/render operations expose or persist a partially-mutated cache. - Storage writes fail under size/quota pressure despite unlimitedStorage, or oversized full-window JPEG data URLs cause excessive turnover. - A data URL remains present but fails to decode/load; TabCard currently has no thumbnail image-error recovery. - A tab lifecycle event incorrectly calls evictThumbnail for a tab that still exists. Constraints: - chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab can capture only the currently active tab in a specified window. Do not silently activate background tabs. - Do not add debugger, tabCapture, desktopCapture, offscreen-page, sessions, or remote page-fetching permissions. - Never delete or replace a valid cached thumbnail merely because a refresh attempt failed. Acceptance criteria: - Reproduce the in-session transition from visible thumbnails to placeholders under repeated automatic captures, long-running sessions, many tabs, byte-limit pressure, entry-limit pressure, tab close/reopen, discarded/frozen tabs, navigation, storage failures, and image decode/load failures. - Capture before/after evidence for current live tab IDs, thumb_* keys, thumbnailCacheAccess metadata, stored byte counts, pruning decisions, and relevant tab lifecycle events so the actual deletion path is proven. - Fix the confirmed loss path. Pruning must delete orphaned/closed-tab thumbnails before entries for live tabs, keep access metadata consistent with stored keys, and avoid leaving partial mutations visible after concurrent operations. - If full-resolution capture size is causing turnover, resize captures to an appropriate thumbnail resolution before storage and use accurate stored-byte accounting. Preserve sufficient quality for cards/lightbox without retaining full-window images unnecessarily. - Define deterministic behavior if live-tab thumbnails alone exceed the configured cap; do not silently collapse most of the board to placeholders after each new capture. - Add thumbnail error handling so a corrupt/undecodable entry is diagnosed, removed safely, and rendered as an honest placeholder without breaking the card. - Opportunistically recapture missing thumbnails when affected tabs naturally become active or complete loading while still active, with per-window deduplication and bounded retry/backoff. Do not claim inactive tabs can be captured without activation. - Preserve a valid previous thumbnail after every failed refresh. - Add regression tests for the diagnosed in-session loss path, live-tab protection, metadata reconciliation, byte accounting, image failure, retry limits, and no-focus-change behavior. - Run the full Node suite and JavaScript syntax checks.

title: Investigate blank thumbnails and add non-intrusive lazy refresh

activity.content:
## Result

Confirmed the in-session loss path: the cache pruned a metadata-only global LRU without checking current Chrome tab IDs. Crossing 200 entries or 50 MB therefore deleted older thumbnails for still-open tabs, matching the observed old placeholders/new survivor pattern. It also removed prior entries before the incoming storage write, so a quota/write failure could leave a partially deleted cache. Full-window JPEG storage accelerated byte pressure.

## Fix

- Reconciled `thumb_*` values and `thumbnailCacheAccess` on every save, recalculating actual UTF-8 stored bytes and serializing the complete cache mutation.
- Protected all live-tab thumbnails. Closed/orphaned entries are pruned first; if live entries alone exceed a limit, the limit is a deterministic soft cap rather than silently deleting live screenshots.
- Made the incoming thumbnail plus reconciled metadata write succeed before orphan cleanup. Failed refresh, resize, focus guard, or storage writes preserve the prior valid thumbnail.
- Resized captures to a maximum 960�600 JPEG before storage and rechecked the active tab after processing.
- Added per-window deduplicated lazy recovery when a missing tab naturally becomes active or completes loading while active. It never activates a tab and is bounded to three attempts with 750/1500 ms backoff. Existing thumbnails are not recaptured merely on activation; completed navigation refreshes once.
- Added card image-error handling that immediately renders an honest letter placeholder and compare-and-removes only the exact corrupt cached value, protecting a newer concurrent replacement.
- Added structured cache/lifecycle diagnostics covering live tab IDs, stored keys, metadata keys, byte totals, prune decisions, and removal/load events.
- Mirrored every runtime change into `meridian-extension`; no permissions were added.

## Regression coverage

Added deterministic coverage for entry and byte pressure, live soft-cap behavior, orphan-first pruning, metadata reconciliation, accurate byte accounting, concurrent saves, incoming write/removal failures, close/removal lifecycle, discarded/frozen/navigation events, focus races, capture resizing and decode failures, image load errors, compare-and-remove safety, retry bounds, and no-focus-change behavior.

## Validation

- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: **107 passed, 0 failed**
- `node --check` for every JavaScript file: **passed**
- Packaged source parity: **passed**
- `git diff --check`: **passed**
- Commit: `8c97ad0 Protect live thumbnails and add lazy recovery`

Reviewer rework required: Eliminate the cross-context removal race. TabCard currently performs a read/compare/remove in the page context while background capture writes through a different module-local queue, so a new thumbnail can be deleted between the comparison and removal. Route conditional removal through the background worker so thumbnail mutations share one serialized context. Also gate/remove the per-save diagnostic dumps and log counts only when debugging. Add a regression for a save racing a failed-image cleanup.

## Result

Completed the reviewer-requested hardening for the thumbnail-loss fix.

- Routed corrupt-image conditional cleanup from `TabCard` to the background service worker via `REMOVE_THUMBNAIL_IF_MATCHES`. Capture saves and failed-image cleanup now use the same background `thumbnailCacheAccess` mutation queue, eliminating the cross-context read/compare/remove race that could delete a newly saved replacement.
- Kept compare-and-remove semantics: cleanup removes only the exact failed data URL and leaves a newer thumbnail intact.
- Gated cache-decision diagnostics behind explicit `DEBUG_THUMBNAILS` mode and reduced debug payloads to counts and byte totals instead of tab IDs, storage keys, and removal key lists.
- Mirrored runtime changes into `meridian-extension`.
- Updated the card error regression to verify background routing and added a save-versus-failed-image-cleanup race regression.

## Validation

- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: **113 passed, 0 failed**

- Worktree: **clean**

Additional rework after live testing: thumbnails still disappear. Implement durable IndexedDB blob storage/migration, preserve cached data on render errors, retry display before showing a placeholder, and mark failed thumbnails for replacement on natural activation rather than deleting them.

Implemented a durable, non-destructive thumbnail cache rework in both source and the running `meridian-extension/` mirror.

- Added IndexedDB-backed JPEG blob storage with reusable `blob:` display URLs; `unlimitedStorage` applies to the extension-local database.
- Migrates existing `chrome.storage.local` thumbnail data URLs into IndexedDB instead of dropping them.
- Preserves the last-known-good blob when an image fails to render.
- Retries a failed image once, then shows a placeholder and marks the thumbnail for replacement on the tab's next natural activation; it no longer deletes the stored thumbnail.
- New captures are decoded/validated before replacing the durable record.
- Cache pruning still protects live tabs and removes both image data and metadata when a tab closes.
- Updated the custom-background IndexedDB schema version, runtime render notifications, privacy/store documentation, runtime mirror, and regressions.

Validation: 117/117 Node tests pass; all runtime JavaScript syntax checks pass; source/runtime parity passes; non-Tasker diff check is clean.
